title: No Measurable Benefit from Verifier‑Assisted Generate→Validate→Repair under Shared‑Initial Generation: A Preregistered Emulation Study
abstract: We preregistered and autonomously executed a paired emulation study (study‑cnd‑2026‑001) that tested whether a verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline increases oracle pass rates for LLM‑produced network configurations on vendor‑diverse emulated NetOps intent→configuration tasks. The frozen design used paired evaluation (Npairs=200), generation semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one generated candidate consumed by both conditions), declared model gpt‑5‑mini, a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and a repair budget ≤1 call/task. Execution produced 200 complete pairs (400 episodes), model_calls_used=200, and repair calls invoked=0. Outcome: baseline = 200/200 oracle passes; guarded = 200/200 oracle passes; absolute paired difference = 0.00 (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.00,0.00]; McNemar two‑sided p=1.00). The null result is design‑bound: because a single shared candidate per pair passed the deterministic oracle in every case, the guarded repair stage was never exercised. We release the full audited artifact bundle (preregistration, prompts, raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, execution manifest and SHA‑256 digests) and interpret the run‑level null result as a ceiling effect caused by the preregistered shared generation semantics and high oracle coverage. We provide artifact‑anchored recommendations to obtain informative comparisons in future evaluations (independent sampling, calibrated task difficulty, larger repair budgets, and validator stress tests).

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are being explored as intent→configuration agents for NetOps because they can translate high‑level operator intents into vendor CLI sequences. However, operational deployment raises a central reliability question: can verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair workflows reduce misconfiguration risk relative to unconstrained generation? We preregistered a confirmatory paired experiment to answer this question under a narrowly specified, auditable design. The preregistration (study‑cnd‑2026‑001; SHA‑256 a8969ac01f3b1bb7585872c58a92f72d0752160dd4e6e01cbafbfe0d15073ad2) fixed model, validator, repair budget, stopping rules, and—critically—the generation semantics: shared_initial_candidate (one candidate generated per pair and consumed by both conditions). This sentence is intentionally explicit: shared_initial_candidate produces one generator call per pair and therefore can prevent the repair pathway from being exercised when the shared candidate satisfies the oracle. The present manuscript reports the autonomous run, archived artifacts, and an artifact‑grounded explanation for the observed null outcome.
sections.related_work: Prior NetOps LLM work covers intent translation, constrained generation, validator‑assisted pipelines, and interactive disambiguation. Representative verified artifacts include MeshAgent (constraint‑based adaptation for NetOps; Zhou et al.), NetConfEval (intent→configuration benchmarks; Wang et al.), and verifier‑grounded repair workflows in DSL/program domains (Ding, StruSpec). Those works motivate verifier‑assisted repair but do not provide preregistered, artifact‑frozen paired evaluations with deterministic oracles and explicit generation semantics. Our run differs by (1) preregistration of the paired estimand and generation semantics, (2) complete archival of every prompt/response/provider trace/validator trace with SHA‑256 digests, and (3) autonomous execution and analysis per the frozen plan.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design. The preregistered study (study‑cnd‑2026‑001; preregistration SHA‑256 a8969ac01f3b1bb7585872c58a92f72d0752160dd4e6e01cbafbfe0d15073ad2) defined the primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Confirmatory sample: 200 paired tasks (400 episodes). Task bank: four protocol buckets (BGP, OSPF, ACL, VLAN) × 50 pairs each; per‑protocol vendor allocation Cisco=17, Juniper=17, Arista=16 (totals Cisco=68, Juniper=68, Arista=64). Complexity: per protocol 25 simple / 25 complex. Model and adapter. Declared model gpt‑5‑mini called via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter; model configuration artifact: execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Generation semantics (frozen). The experiment used shared_initial_candidate: exactly one generator call per pair produced the candidate consumed by both baseline and guarded pipelines. Repair budget and validator. Repair budget ≤1 repair call per task (preregistered). Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 scored candidates against explicit intent constraints and an emulated network oracle. Stopping and missingness. Stopping rule: execute all planned pairs unless provider/model identifier drift occurs, in which case affected pairs are flagged (no drift occurred). Primary analysis required complete pairs; infrastructure failures exclude pairs from primary analysis and are logged.
sections.results: Execution accounting (artifact‑backed). The autonomous run executed per the preregistered plan and archived all artifacts (execution/execution_manifest.json contains full per‑file SHA‑256s). Planned_episode_count=400; completed_episode_count=400; failed_episode_count=0; model_calls_used=200 (one shared generation per pair). Reparations: repair calls invoked=0 (the repair stage did not execute because the validator accepted every shared candidate). Confirmatory outcome (artifact: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c): baseline_success_count=200/200 (100%); guarded_success_count=200/200 (100%); paired contingency n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0. Point estimate: absolute paired difference = 0.00. Inference: paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI [0.00,0.00] (bootstrap_resamples=10,000, seed=1729) and exact McNemar two‑sided p=1.00. Representative examples. Validator trace excerpts (archived) show parsed commands, normalized configuration, and validator verdicts; for example execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 eaf96aec12c30860a6fd70987289cc71104134a3330b99c7e024f244dbd35c1b) documents a medium‑difficulty shutdown_configure_restore task whose shared candidate satisfied all oracle predicates and therefore required no repair.
sections.discussion: Causal interpretation: the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics produced one generated candidate per pair that both conditions consumed. In this execution that candidate passed the deterministic validator in every case; accordingly the guarded repair stage had no opportunity to act and the paired comparison is uninformative about repair efficacy under independent generation or more adversarial failure conditions. The observed null result is thus a design‑bound ceiling effect rather than a general negative result about verifier‑assisted repair. Threats to validity (artifact‑grounded). Internal validity: the generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate) fixed generator variance across conditions and reduced the number of model calls (model_calls_used=200). Construct validity: the deterministic validator covers explicit intent predicates recorded per task, but oracle blind spots remain possible; validator coverage diagnostics were recorded (analysis/contamination_summary.csv). External validity: single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) and emulated tasks limit generalizability to other models or production devices. Conclusion validity: the paired design yielded perfect concordance (n11=200), which prevents estimation of repair effect in this run.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed an auditable paired emulation run that compared verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair to unconstrained generation under frozen shared_initial_candidate semantics. Both conditions achieved 200/200 oracle passes; repair was never triggered. The null result is traceable to the preregistered generation semantics and high oracle coverage (artifact backs: execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/*). We release the full artifact bundle (prompts, raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, scoring files, analysis artifacts) with per‑file SHA‑256 digests to enable reproducible reruns and alternative executions (e.g., independent generation or expanded repair budgets). Practical next steps supported directly by the archived artifacts: re‑execute with independent sampling per condition, calibrate task difficulty to force some initial failures, increase repair budget to allow iterative repair, and run across multiple model instances to assess generality.

disclosure_statement:
Mandatory Disclosure Statement (artifact‑backed):
- Initial master prompt (immutable artifact): provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). This master prompt defined the autonomous researcher role and autonomy boundary and launched the post‑lock autonomous run. The Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) before the autonomy lock; all subsequent literature search, experiment design, execution, analysis, and manuscript generation were performed autonomously after the lock per the master prompt.
- Preregistration (frozen): study id study‑cnd‑2026‑001; preregistration artifact SHA‑256 = a8969ac01f3b1bb7585872c58a92f72d0752160dd4e6e01cbafbfe0d15073ad2. The preregistration froze estimands, sampling plan, generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate), declared model, validator, repair budget, stopping rules, missingness policy, and analysis executor.
- Declared LLM and adapter: model gpt‑5‑mini called via hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model configuration artifact execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). All provider call traces are archived under execution/provider_calls/ and hashed; raw responses are under execution/responses/ and hashed. Execution accounting (model_calls_used=200, repair_calls_invoked=0) is recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json.
- Preregistered generation semantics: shared_initial_candidate (one generator call per pair; the same candidate consumed by baseline and guarded). This choice is central to the observed outcome: because the single shared candidate per pair passed the deterministic oracle in every case, repair was never invoked. The generation semantics and per‑pair provider call artifacts are archived in execution/* with SHA‑256 digests recorded in the execution manifest.
- Validator and scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 performed objective oracle checks; representative scoring artifacts include execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 eaf96aec12c30860a6fd70987289cc71104134a3330b99c7e024f244dbd35c1b). All validator traces and scoring JSON files are archived and hashed.
- Repair policy and usage: preregistered maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; actual repair_calls_invoked = 0 in this run (artifact: execution/execution_manifest.json). Repair prompts and traces would have been archived if any repair call occurred.
- Analysis and reproducibility: analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1 with paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) and exact McNemar test. Analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c; analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256 = 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951) and the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) contain full per‑file SHA‑256 digests enabling deterministic verification. Deterministic reconciliation artifact is analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA‑256 799b23b993fcc9c04fc4d0a375e975937bc11d9f8c6595d43dce94375411d174).
- Human role: prior to the autonomy lock the Research Director selected the topic family and approved the master prompt and pre‑lock infrastructure development. No human performed manual substantive editing or selective improvement of the manuscript after the autonomy lock; all manuscript content derives from the autonomous post‑lock pipeline. Pre‑lock development artifacts were not used as empirical evidence unless reproduced under the frozen post‑lock workflow.
- Deviations and failures: no provider/model drift occurred during the run; no episodes failed due to infrastructure. All planned pairs were executed and archived. The absence of repair invocation is an empirical fact recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json and in the scoring artifacts.
- Availability: the complete artifact bundle (preregistration, prompts, model calls, provider traces, validator traces, scoring files, execution manifest, analysis artifacts and SHA‑256 digests) is archived and referenced throughout this manuscript; specific artifact paths and SHA‑256 values are listed in the execution manifest and analysis artifacts mentioned above.
limitations: The preregistered shared_initial_candidate generation semantics produced one generated candidate per pair; because every shared candidate passed the deterministic oracle, the guarded repair pathway was never exercised (repair_calls_invoked = 0). The run therefore cannot measure repair efficacy under independent sampling.
Single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) and single deterministic validator limit external generalizability; multi‑model replication is needed to assess generality.
Emulation with a deterministic validator and synthetic tasks does not fully capture production device heterogeneity or nondeterministic runtime behaviors.
Repair budget was intentionally restricted (≤1 call/task) by the preregistration; richer iterative repair policies were not explored in this run.
Oracle blind spots remain possible despite deterministic validation; validator coverage diagnostics are archived but cannot prove exhaustiveness.
